lines.text: stretto. Read ahead of your agent.
An agent spends an LLM turn on every tool call, and those turns are most of what it costs.
But many of those turns are decided before they start. The first result named both orders, so the next two reads were fixed by the tools, not by the customer.
stretto makes those reads for the agent. They ride in the same tool result, so the agent skips those turns. A wrong read costs only tokens, and changes nothing: stretto only reads.
First, record. stretto-proxy wraps any MCP server, forwards every message, and records each session.
Then learn. stretto counts which reads follow which calls, and where each argument came from. The flow is a file you review like code.
Then serve. After each call, the flow's lookups ride in the result the agent already gets. No new tool, and no change to the prompt.
A lookup is made when the chance that the agent uses it before its next write clears a threshold set by costs, about 0.3. No model is asked: the proxy counts.
Live, on 28 τ²-bench retail and airline tasks, GLM-5.3 took 27.9% fewer LLM turns. In AgentDojo's Slack and travel suites, GLM-5.3 and Claude Haiku 4.5 took 10.1% fewer, with passes unchanged.
To start, install stretto and run stretto init. It prints your host's configuration, and the steps to a served flow. The quickstart runs the whole loop with no key.
stretto. Read ahead of your agent.
